findings.title: Computed Zod keys do not validate or preserve expiry fields
findings.body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema produces a literal property name (normally "[object Object]"), not a wildcard for response properties. Both computed keys therefore collide, and this z.object also strips unrecognized properties such as expires_in, expiry_date and refresh_token. With credential sharing enabled, valid refresh responses lose their expiry and refresh token; Zoom then computes a NaN expiry and other integrations cannot persist usable refreshed credentials. Use explicit supported fields or a passthrough schema with appropriate validation.

findings.title: Do not replace omitted refresh tokens with a placeholder
findings.body: This helper injects the literal string "refresh_token" whenever a response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly allows refresh_token to be omitted and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials, so this now overwrites the real stored refresh token with an unusable placeholder. The following refresh fails and the user must reconnect. Preserve the existing token when the provider does not return a replacement.

findings.title: Persist parsed Google credentials rather than the safeParse result
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result envelope, { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous schema.parse returned the credential object itself. Writing this result directly to credential.key stores the envelope instead of access_token, refresh_token and expiry_date at the top level. The next GoogleCalendarService construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse, breaking calendar access after a refresh even with syncing disabled. Store the result's data.

findings.title: Normalize sync responses to the contracts expected by SDK callers
findings.body: The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but several callers still expect the result of their original refresh function: Google and both Zoho integrations read response.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly from a decoded SDK object. A native Response has none of those properties, regardless of its JSON body, so enabling syncing makes these refreshes throw or store invalid tokens. Decode and adapt the sync response for these callers, or change them to consume a consistent response contract.

findings.title: Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint
findings.body: The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is a Cal.com user ID, but this call passes credentialId. Consequently the external endpoint receives a credential table primary key as calcomUserId instead of the owner's ID. Since those IDs are unrelated, it can fail to find the account or return another user's credentials when the numbers coincide. Carry credential.userId through the refresh method and pass that value; team credentials should retain the null-user fallback.

findings.title: Import Prisma before using it in Salesforce refresh
findings.body: The new refresh path calls prisma.credential.update, but this module does not import or declare prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws ReferenceError on every Salesforce client initialization. Import the Prisma client used by the other integration services.

findings.title: Send the Zoom app slug rather than its integration directory name
findings.body: The refresh request sends appSlug: "zoomvideo", but Zoom credentials are registered with appId "zoom" and the OAuth callback also uses the slug "zoom". An external app store routing refreshes by the supplied appSlug cannot match this request to the Zoom app, preventing refreshes for synced Zoom credentials. Send "zoom" consistently.
